CIVILIAN RESILIENCE / SERVICE-CONTINUITY MODEL / 100 KM PLANNING VIEW

Supplementary support & unmet-need probability

Where could civilian support (welfare, shelter, transport, information) fall short in an emergency? Choose a scenario, then read the map and charts. Probabilities are simulated, not measured.

ON THIS PAGEAdjust the scenario on the right → map and charts update

Summary. Four headline numbers for the chosen scenario: the average chance a cell runs short of civilian support, how many cells are high-need, the average after extra support, and the spread between cells.

02 / Supplementary capacity

Illustrative distribution of generic multi-purpose support teams across four abstract planning sectors; not real dispatch instructions.

Modelled shortfall reduction—

Example support: welfare check-ins, accessible transport, portable information points, drinking water, temporary shelter coordination and continuity of care.

03 / Probabilistic method

Scenario-dependent stochastic draws estimate cell probabilities. A random-walk Metropolis chain then samples a spatial density π(x,y) proportional to those modeled probabilities.

0.18
ACCEPTANCE—Metropolis chain
RETAINED SAMPLES—after 350-step burn-in

π(x,y) = P(gap | scenario, synthetic assumptions), normalized over the model grid to guide the walker. The chain is a visualization technique, not a trained prediction model.

History & outlook. Real events in the region since 2016 that informed the scenario types, and planning priorities for 2027–2030. These sources shape the scenarios, not the percentages.

Historical review / 2016–2026

2017 · Northern storm

Severe wind events caused safety warnings and disruptions in the Hamburg region.

Hamburg authority ↗
2018–2022 · Heat stress

Repeated hot periods across Germany increased public-health risks and strained infrastructure.

German Environment Agency ↗
2021 · Ahr floods

Flash flooding demonstrated how transport, communications and response capacity can fail together.

UBA assessment ↗
2022 · Severe storms

Hamburg's storm and surge data record major events, including Storm Zeynep.

Hamburg climate indicators ↗
2024 · Extreme rain

Hamburg Wasser published citywide heavy-rain hazard mapping following repeated major rain events.

Hamburg Wasser ↗
2025–2026 · Preparedness

Hamburg implemented a heat action plan and maintains guidance for storms, power loss and cyber incidents.

Hamburg crisis preparation ↗
Background: Hamburg storm-surge guidance · Hamburg heat plan · UBA emergency-responder impacts

Forward outlook / 2027–2030

01 · Strengthen flood & storm response

Plan flexible overflow shelters and alternate warning channels for high-demand weather episodes.

02 · Reach residents needing extra assistance

Exercise multilingual communications, mobility assistance and proactive care check-ins.

03 · Prepare for multi-service disruption

Test offline coordination, welfare continuity and cross-jurisdictional mutual aid.

04 · Make allocation auditable

Replace all synthetic features with consented, aggregated public-service data before operational use.

These are planning priorities inferred from historical conditions, not predictions of attack objectives, event dates or target locations.

PHOTOREALISTIC 3D · ONE-TIME SETUP

Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles

Streams Google's photorealistic 3D city (the same data as Google Earth) through CesiumJS, with the drone attack, defences and protected sites drawn on top at true altitude. Paste one of these:

  1. Google Maps API key with the Map Tiles API enabled (Google Cloud console → APIs & Services). Billing must be switched on; Google includes a monthly free allowance.
  2. Cesium ion access token (free account at ion.cesium.com, add the "Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles" asset). Ion serves the same Google tiles.

The key is kept in this browser only, never written into the file. In Google Cloud, restrict it to the Map Tiles API and set a daily quota. A key restricted to websites will not work from a local file. Needs internet; Google's logo and data credits stay visible as required.

How do I interpret this demonstration?
💬 Demo Assistant
Local Demonstration Assistant Inspector ❐

This interface uses a fixed JavaScript simulation and a rule-based explanation panel. It is not connected to any external AI platform, satellite intelligence or live data source.

Try: “show radar”, “go to score”, “what is the cost”, “show agents”, or “explain this phase”.

Ask about the simulated scene, metrics or navigation. Responses are scripted and use the local scenario state.

How to use this demo

  1. ▶ Play runs a notional 1,000-drone attack on Hamburg in 8 scenes. Drag the bottom timeline, or use ‹ › to step through the scenes.
  2. Overview · Aerial · Street (top bar) are three cameras on the same area and the same attack: the map, a top-down satellite view and a tilted 3D view. Each can zoom from the whole region down to street level.
  3. ☰ Scenario opens response plans, logs and chat. ▤ Details shows counters and cost per kill. Tap ✕ or anywhere outside a panel to close it.
  4. Maps: drag to pan, pinch or scroll to zoom. In Street view, drag to orbit the camera.

All data is synthetic. Tap ? in the top bar to see this again.

Attack and defence

Set how many drones and cruise missiles attack, which drone types they are, when the main wave starts and what it aims at. Extra waves, blasts and timed response actions are on the Timeline tab. Costs other than Geran-2, altitudes and how well each defence works against each type are notional.
